origin.description: site_config_dir returns full path to the user-specific configuration directory for this application which returns the same path as site data directory in Windows and Mac but a different one for Unix. Typical user-shared data directories are: Mac OS X /Library/Application Support/<AppName>, Unix /usr/local/share:/usr/share/, Win XP C:\Documents and Settings\All Users\Application Data\<AppAuthor>\<AppName>, Vista (Fail! C:\ProgramData is a hidden system directory on Vista.), Win 7 C:\ProgramData\<AppAuthor>\<AppName>. Hidden, but writeable on Win 7. Unix also specifies a separate location for user-shared configuration data in $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS. Unix: /etc/xdg/<AppName>, in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME if defined. For Unix, this returns the first default. Set the multipath=TRUE to guarantee returning all directories.
origin.usage: site_config_dir(appname = NULL, appauthor = appname, version = NULL, multipath = FALSE, expand = TRUE, os = NULL)

arguments.name: appname
arguments.text: is the name of application. If NULL, just the system directory is returned.

arguments.name: appauthor
arguments.text: (only required and used on Windows) is the name of the appauthor or distributing body for this application. Typically it is the owning company name. This falls back to appname.

arguments.name: version
arguments.text: is an optional version path element to append to the path. You might want to use this if you want multiple versions of your app to be able to run independently. If used, this would typically be "<major>.<minor>". Only applied when appname is not NULL.

arguments.name: multipath
arguments.text: is an optional parameter only applicable to *nix which indicates that the entire list of data dirs should be returned. By default, the first directory is returned.

arguments.name: expand
arguments.text: If TRUE (the default) will expand the R_LIBS specifiers with their equivalents. See R_LIBS() for list of all possibly specifiers.

arguments.name: os
arguments.text: Operating system whose conventions are used to construct the requested directory. Possible values are "win", "mac", "unix". If NULL (the default) then the current OS will be used.

origin.details: Do not use this on Windows. See the note above for why.
origin.value: Path to the site configuration directory, or on Unix with multipath=TRUE a character vector of paths.

translation.description: Return the site-wide configuration directory for an application. Windows and macOS follow the same layout as site data. Unix reads XDG_CONFIG_DIRS, default /etc/xdg, and returns the first entry unless multipath is true.
translation.usage: site_config_dir(appname=None, appauthor=appname, version=None, multipath=False, expand=True, os=None)

arguments.name: appname
arguments.text: Application directory name. None returns only the system config directory.

arguments.name: appauthor
arguments.text: Windows author directory. Omitted, it uses appname. None leaves that component out.

arguments.name: version
arguments.text: Optional path piece. Ignored, with a warning, when appname is None. expand rewrites %V, %v, %p, %o, %a, and %%.

arguments.name: multipath
arguments.text: On unix only, when true return a list of paths for every entry in XDG_CONFIG_DIRS.

arguments.name: expand
arguments.text: When true, replace R_LIBS specifiers in version. A number 0 is false and any other number is true.

arguments.name: os
arguments.text: win, mac, or unix. None uses this process: Windows, Darwin, or unix.

translation.details: Pieces are joined with the platform separator. NULL is dropped and an empty string stays. On this system a missing Windows folder variable is <USERPROFILE>, and the simulated Windows path still uses this system's separator.
translation.value: One path string, or on unix with multipath a list of strings.
